title: Cross-Commons Identity Key
description: The semi-rigid rule of the MADFAM hyperobject commons (RFC 0038 §9): one physical thing may exist as TWO cartridges in two commons — a SOLID one (Yantra4D, a printed/machined body) and a SOFT one (Fashion Cabinet, the same thing understood as cloth or as a garment component). A pair record declares that those two slugs are the same object, and names the material identity under which the equivalence holds. Without the material identity the claim is unfalsifiable: a chainmail panel printed in TPU-95A drapes as cloth, the same geometry printed in PLA does not.

spec_version.description: Version of THIS identity-key contract the record is written against. Absent means 1.

identity_id.description: Stable slug for the pair itself, unique across the commons. Conventionally the shared physical noun, e.g. 'chainmail-panel'.

solid.description: The rigid-body side — a Yantra4D cartridge that renders a solid.

soft.description: The soft-goods side — a Fashion Cabinet cartridge (a garment, a notion, or a fabric card).

material_identity.description: The material under which the two sides are the SAME object. The pairing is only claimed for this material.

label.description: Human-readable name of the paired object.

notes.description: Why the two sides are one object, and where the equivalence stops.

repo.description: Which commons the cartridge lives in.

slug.description: The cartridge's slug within that repo — its project.json project.slug (or, for a fabric card, its fabric.slug).

kind.description: What the slug names in that repo. Defaults to 'cartridge'.

soft_material.description: The Fashion Cabinet fabric-card slug (materials/<slug>/material.json) describing the object AS CLOTH.

solid_material.description: The Yantra4D material slug (materials/<slug>/material.json) the solid is printed in.

equivalence.description: How far the identity holds. 'same_object' = one physical thing, two descriptions. 'derived' = the soft side is produced from the solid side (or vice versa) but is not the identical body. Defaults to 'same_object'.
